disclaimer: This assistant provides educational guidance only and is not a diagnosis. For severe, persistent, or worsening symptoms, consult a licensed doctor.

conditions.name: Common Cold
conditions.overview: A mild viral upper-respiratory infection spread by airborne droplets.
followUp: Are symptoms worse in morning or evening?
Any recent travel or sick contacts?
homeCare: Drink warm fluids (tea, soup) to soothe throat and hydrate.
Take over-the-counter pain relievers (ibuprofen 400-600mg every 6-8 hours).
Use saline nasal drops or neti pot for congestion.
Get 7-9 hours of sleep to support immune function.
Gargle with salt water (1/2 tsp salt in 8oz warm water) 3x daily.
doctorWhen: Symptoms last longer than 10 days or worsen after 5 days.
High fever (>102°F) or severe throat pain.
Cough produces colored phlegm or breathing becomes difficult.
Signs of secondary infection (ear pain, sinus pressure).
conditions.timeline: Monitor for 3–5 days. Improve by day 5–7, resolve by day 10.

conditions.name: Flu-like Illness
conditions.overview: Viral infection (likely influenza) causing systemic symptoms and fever.
followUp: Any close contacts with confirmed flu?
homeCare: Rest: Take 3–5 days off work or school to prevent spread.
Hydration: Drink 8-10 glasses of water, warm tea, or broth daily.
Fever management: Use acetaminophen (500mg every 6 hours) or ibuprofen (400mg every 6-8 hours).
Humidifier: Use a cool-mist humidifier to ease congestion and cough.
Nutrition: Eat light foods (broth, rice, eggs) when appetite returns.
doctorWhen: Fever persists beyond 5 days or spikes again after 24 hours fever-free.
Difficulty breathing or chest pain develops.
Severe weakness, confusion, or persistent vomiting.
High-risk groups (elderly, pregnant, chronic illness).
conditions.timeline: Peak symptoms days 1–3. Gradual improvement by day 5. Full recovery 7–10 days.

conditions.name: Acute Gastritis / Acidity
conditions.overview: Stomach lining inflammation causing burning sensation, often acid-reflux related.
followUp: Any recent spicy or fatty meals?
homeCare: Avoid: Spicy, fried, fatty foods; caffeine; alcohol; chocolate.
Eat: Small, frequent meals (every 2–3 hours) of bland foods.
Antacids: Take over-the-counter antacids (Tums, Rolaids) after meals.
Elevate: Sleep with head elevated 30–45 degrees.
Wait 2–3 hours after eating before lying down.
doctorWhen: Pain is severe or recurs after 3 days of home care.
Vomiting persists or contains blood.
Difficulty swallowing or signs of bleeding.
conditions.timeline: Rapid relief with antacids (30 min–2 hours). Full recovery 1–3 days.

conditions.name: Food Poisoning
conditions.overview: Acute digestive infection from contaminated food or water.
followUp: What did you eat in last 12 hours?
Anyone else sick after same meal?
homeCare: Oral Rehydration: Start with small sips of water, coconut water, or sports drinks.
Electrolyte solution: Mix 6 tsp sugar + 1/2 tsp salt in 1L water; drink 200ml every 1–2 hours.
Food progression: Start with crackers, toast, rice; avoid dairy and high-fiber foods for 24 hours.
Rest: Avoid strenuous activity; let your body heal.
Track output: Monitor urine color (dark = dehydration).
doctorWhen: Severe dehydration signs: dark urine, dizziness, no urination for 8+ hours.
Diarrhea contains blood or lasts >3 days.
High fever (>102°F) or severe abdominal pain.
Signs of sepsis: rapid heartbeat, confusion.
conditions.timeline: Vomiting subsides 12–24 hours. Diarrhea resolves 24–72 hours. Weakness may persist 1 week.

conditions.name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
conditions.overview: Bacterial infection of bladder or urethra causing burning urination.
homeCare: Hydration: Drink 2–3 liters of water daily to flush bacteria.
Cranberry juice: May help prevent recurrence (not cure active infection).
Urination: Don't hold it; empty bladder fully each time.
Heat: Apply warm compress to lower abdomen for pain relief.
Hygiene: Wipe front to back; avoid douching.
doctorWhen: Symptoms persist beyond 24 hours despite hydration.
Fever or back pain (suggests kidney involvement).
Pregnancy or signs of severe infection.
Inability to urinate despite urge.
conditions.timeline: With antibiotics, improvement within 24–48 hours. Full resolution 3–7 days.

conditions.name: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever)
conditions.overview: Allergic reaction causing nasal and respiratory inflammation.
homeCare: Antihistamines: Take cetirizine (Zyrtec) or loratadine (Claritin) daily.
Nasal spray: Use saline or corticosteroid nasal spray.
Avoid triggers: Keep windows closed during high pollen; shower after outdoor time.
HEPA filter: Use in bedroom to reduce allergen exposure.
Decongestants: Use only short-term (3–5 days max) to avoid rebound.
doctorWhen: Symptoms interfere with sleep or work despite OTC treatment.
Wheezing or signs of asthma develop.
Sinus infection suspected (thick colored discharge, facial pain).
conditions.timeline: OTC meds provide relief within 30 min–1 hour. Duration depends on allergen exposure.

conditions.name: Bronchitis
conditions.overview: Inflammation of large airways producing persistent productive cough.
homeCare: Humidifier: Use cool-mist to ease airway irritation.
Expectorant: Take guaifenesin (Mucinex) to thin mucus.
Cough drops: Use honey lozenges or sugar-free cough drops.
Warm fluids: Tea with honey and lemon soothes throat.
Avoid irritants: No smoking or secondhand smoke; avoid dusty environments.
Rest: Sleep with extra pillows to ease breathing.
doctorWhen: Cough persists beyond 3 weeks or worsens.
Coughing up blood or dark/green phlegm.
Severe breathlessness at rest or chest pain.
High fever (>102°F) for >3 days.
conditions.timeline: Acute phase 1–2 weeks. Cough may linger 3–4 weeks. Preventive: quit smoking, avoid irritants.

conditions.name: Bacterial Throat Infection (Strep)
conditions.overview: Strep throat causing severe throat pain and swollen tonsils.
followUp: Any pus or white patches on tonsils?
homeCare: Pain relief: Acetaminophen (500mg) or ibuprofen (400mg) every 6–8 hours.
Throat soothing: Gargle with salt water (1/2 tsp salt in 8oz warm water) every 2–3 hours.
Lozenges: Use throat lozenges with numbing agents.
Soft foods: Eat ice cream, applesauce, pudding; avoid hot foods.
Rest: Adequate sleep supports immune response.
Hydration: Sip warm tea or room-temperature liquids.
doctorWhen: Throat pain is severe or persists >48 hours.
Fever >102°F or difficulty swallowing.
Severe headache, stiff neck, or rash.
Any previous rheumatic fever (needs urgent care).
conditions.timeline: With antibiotics, pain relief within 24–48 hours. Resolution 7–10 days. Contagious 24 hours after starting antibiotics.

conditions.name: Migraine Headache
conditions.overview: Severe throbbing headache, often one-sided with nausea.
homeCare: Rest: Lie down in dark, quiet room; close curtains.
Temperature: Apply cold compress to head or warm compress to neck.
Medication: Use ibuprofen (400mg) or naproxen (220mg) at first symptom.
Hydration: Drink water; dehydration worsens migraines.
Avoid triggers: Identify and avoid personal triggers (caffeine, alcohol, MSG, skipped meals).
Acupressure: Press between thumb and forefinger for 5–10 minutes.
doctorWhen: Migraine pattern changes (frequency, severity, location).
Worst headache of your life or sudden-onset severe headache.
Vision loss, weakness, or difficulty speaking.
Fever or stiff neck accompanies headache.
conditions.timeline: Rest and meds provide relief in 1–6 hours. Full resolution 4–72 hours. Prevention is key (lifestyle, stress management).

conditions.name: Viral Gastroenteritis (Stomach Flu)
conditions.overview: Viral stomach infection causing vomiting, diarrhea, and cramping.
followUp: Any close contacts with similar illness?
homeCare: Oral Rehydration: Sip water, coconut water, or sports drinks in small amounts (2–3 oz every 15 min).
Electrolyte balance: Use WHO rehydration solution if available.
Progress to food: Start crackers → toast → rice → broth → bland meals over 24 hours.
Avoid: Dairy, fatty foods, high-fiber foods, and acidic drinks for 48 hours.
Rest: Separate bathroom use; wash hands after toilet.
Monitor: Track hydration; dark urine indicates dehydration.
doctorWhen: Severe dehydration (dizziness, no urination >8 hours, dark urine).
Blood in vomit or stool.
Abdominal pain is severe or worsening.
Symptoms persist >3 days.
conditions.timeline: Acute phase 12–24 hours. Improvement by 48 hours. Full recovery 2–3 days. Contagious for 24–48 hours after last symptom.

conditions.name: Tension Headache
conditions.overview: Mild to moderate tension in head, scalp, or neck; most common headache type.
homeCare: Relaxation: Practice deep breathing, progressive muscle relaxation.
Heat: Apply heating pad to neck and shoulders for 20 minutes.
Massage: Self-massage temples, neck, and shoulder muscles.
Posture: Correct desk posture; ensure monitor at eye level.
Hydration: Drink water; mild dehydration triggers tension headaches.
Medication: Ibuprofen (400mg) or acetaminophen (500mg) if needed.
doctorWhen: Headaches increase in frequency or severity.
New pattern or accompanied by other symptoms (vision changes, weakness).
Sudden onset severe headache (different from usual).
conditions.timeline: Usually resolve within hours with rest. Recurrent cases benefit from stress management and physical therapy.

conditions.name: Contact Dermatitis (Skin Rash)
conditions.overview: Allergic skin reaction from contact with irritant or allergen.
homeCare: Identify trigger: Avoid suspected irritant (soaps, metals, plants).
Cleanse: Wash affected area gently with fragrance-free soap.
Topical cream: Use hydrocortisone cream (1%) 3x daily.
Cool compress: Apply for 10 minutes to reduce itching.
Avoid scratching: Trim nails; wear soft clothing.
Moisturize: Use fragrance-free lotion after bathing.
doctorWhen: Rash spreads rapidly or involves face/genitals.
Signs of infection (pus, warmth, increasing swelling).
Severe itching disturbs sleep or daily function.
No improvement after 1–2 weeks of self-care.
conditions.timeline: Itching improves 24–48 hours with treatment. Rash fades over 1–3 weeks. Recurrence if trigger re-exposure.

conditions.name: Muscle Strain / Overexertion
conditions.overview: Muscle soreness and pain from new activity or physical strain.
homeCare: Rest: Avoid strenuous activity for 24–48 hours; light movement okay.
Ice: Apply ice pack for 15–20 minutes every 2–3 hours for first 48 hours.
Heat: After 48 hours, apply heat for 15–20 minutes to ease stiffness.
Compression: Use elastic bandage or sleeve for mild compression.
Elevation: Elevate affected limb if swelling.
OTC pain relief: Ibuprofen (400mg) or naproxen (220mg) if needed.
Gradual return: Resume activity slowly over 1–2 weeks.
doctorWhen: Severe pain or inability to move.
Pain worsens after 5 days or doesn't improve after 2 weeks.
Swelling, warmth, or redness (signs of inflammation or infection).
Suspected fracture or severe strain (deformity, extreme pain).
conditions.timeline: Peak soreness 24–48 hours. Improvement begins day 3. Full recovery 3–7 days for mild strain, weeks for severe.

conditions.name: Asthma (Exercise or Allergic)
conditions.overview: Airway narrowing causing wheezing, cough, or shortness of breath.
followUp: Triggered by exercise, allergies, or cold air?
homeCare: Rescue inhaler: Use albuterol inhaler (if prescribed) at first wheeze.
Rest: Stop activity and sit upright.
Slow breathing: Practice deep, slow breathing to calm airways.
Trigger avoidance: Avoid known triggers (allergens, exercise in cold, air pollution).
Humidity: Use humidifier if dry environment triggers symptoms.
Emergency: Call 911 if no improvement after 15 minutes or severe distress.
doctorWhen: First-time wheezing or shortness of breath.
Rescue inhaler not relieving symptoms.
Wheezing accompanied by chest pain or confusion.
Peak flow meter reading significantly lower than baseline.
conditions.timeline: Acute attack resolves 15–30 min with inhaler. Require controller medication if frequent episodes. Prevention is key.

conditions.name: Anxiety or Panic Disorder
conditions.overview: Excessive worry or sudden panic attacks with physical symptoms.
homeCare: Breathing technique: 4–7–8 breathing (breathe 4 counts, hold 7, exhale 8).
Grounding: Use 5 senses (5 things you see, 4 you touch, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, 1 you taste).
Movement: Take a short walk or gentle stretching.
Limit caffeine: Reduce coffee, energy drinks, and sugar.
Sleep: Maintain consistent sleep schedule (7–9 hours).
Therapy: Consider CBT or mindfulness apps (Headspace, Calm).
doctorWhen: Panic attacks are frequent or intensifying.
Anxiety interferes with work, relationships, or quality of life.
Chest pain or shortness of breath is severe (rule out cardiac causes).
First-time panic attack (rule out medical causes).
conditions.timeline: Acute panic attack subsides 5–30 minutes. Anxiety management requires ongoing practice. Therapy/medication effective within weeks.

conditions.name: Sinusitis
conditions.overview: Sinus inflammation causing congestion, facial pain, and sinus pressure.
followUp: Any facial pressure or upper tooth pain?
homeCare: Saline rinse: Use neti pot or saline spray 2–3x daily.
Decongestant: Pseudoephedrine (Sudafed) or oxymetazoline spray (short-term only).
Humidifier: Add moisture to air.
Heat compress: Apply warm compress to sinuses.
Hydration: Drink warm liquids; avoid alcohol.
Sleep elevation: Prop head with extra pillow.
doctorWhen: Symptoms last >10 days or worsen after 5 days.
Severe facial or tooth pain.
High fever (>102°F) or signs of infection.
Vision changes or signs extending to eyes/brain.
conditions.timeline: Self-limited viral sinusitis resolves 5–7 days. Bacterial may require antibiotics, 7–14 days to resolve.

conditions.name: Common Seasonal Allergy
conditions.overview: Seasonal pollen allergy causing nasal and eye symptoms.
followUp: Specific time of year symptoms appear?
homeCare: Antihistamines: Daily cetirizine (Zyrtec) or loratadine (Claritin).
Eye drops: Use antihistamine eye drops if eyes itch.
Trigger avoidance: Stay indoors during high pollen (early morning, windy days).
Shower: Wash hair and change clothes after outdoor time.
HEPA filter: Use in bedroom.
Saline rinse: Rinse nasal passages daily.
doctorWhen: OTC medications ineffective.
Symptoms worsen or trigger asthma-like symptoms.
Consider allergy testing or prescription options.
conditions.timeline: OTC meds provide relief within 1 hour. Season-dependent duration. Complete resolution when pollen dispersal ends.
